title: Curate dependency matrix and remove legacy SDK API shims
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Goal: Reduce runtime surface area and incidental token/cpu costs by curating a cross-language dependency matrix, pinning transitive packages we rely on, and retiring legacy API shims that add allocation and branching overhead at runtime. This ticket covers coordinated language bumps (Python/JS/Go), a compatibility adapter for a 2-week canary, and a migration/comm-deprecation path for customers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dependency matrix (spreadsheet) listing direct + critical transitive deps with minimum supported versions for each language and compatibility notes; 2) PRs that pin/align top 25 transitive deps across SDKs and pass CI; 3) Removal of 3 legacy API shim layers that add 5-15% p50 CPU allocation in benchmarks, with compatibility adapter available; 4) Migration guide + codemod for JS and Python; 5) Canary rollout plan and rollback criteria documented.
updates: 2026-02-25: Kickoff — aligned with PM and Design on non-goals (no API surface expansion). Decided target: cut legacy shims that wrap response objects and normalize back-compat via an optional adapter package.

2026-02-28: Completed initial dependency crawl for all three SDKs. Top transitive offenders identified: serializer libs (2), http adapters (3), and misc logging/metrics libs (4). Exported CSV to Drive.

2026-03-03: Benchmark snapshot against runtime-1.18 baseline on dev-gpu cluster: removing shim layer reduced p50 CPU by ~9% for Python end-to-end generate flow; ~6% improvement in median memory for Node.js on short prompt workloads. Detailed numbers in attachments.

2026-03-05: Design/PM review — agreed to ship compatibility adapter under @redwood/sdk-compat as a temporary package for major customers requiring old fields. Adapter will be deprecated after 2 cycles (by sdk-2026.06).

2026-03-07: Opened three coordinated PRs: python: #4109 (pin transitive deps, remove shim), js: #4127 (codemod + shim removal behind flag), go: #1582 (minor bump + test fixes). CI flakes observed for js-coverage job; investigating.

2026-03-10: Mitigated js coverage flakes by increasing test timeout and pinning axios-transitive to 1.3.1 in lockfile. Re-ran benchmarks: p50 latency unchanged but p95 error rate for long streaming lowered from 0.7% to 0.1%.

2026-03-12: QA checklist created and signed off by eng QA. Canary plan drafted: stage 1 internal (team opt-in), stage 2 limited customer cohort (10 customers), rollback criteria: >2% regressions in p50 or any increase in errors >0.5% above baseline.
Next steps: complete migration docs + codemod, finalize PR gating to require manual approval for canary release, schedule canary for 2026-03-18.
implementation_notes:
- Use dependency matrix to generate automated Dependabot rules for consistent minor bumps.
- Avoid forced major bumps; prefer pin+patch strategy for transient transitive churn.
- Keep legacy response fields available via lightweight adapter that maps old names to new schema without copying large buffers.
- Add CI job to run small benchmark harness on PRs touching runtime-critical shim code.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: accidental breaking change for customers using undocumented shim internals. Mitigation: produce migration codemod and keep adapter package for 2 cycles; add telemetry to detect usage of deprecated fields.
Risk: dependency conflict during minor bumps. Mitigation: run integration test matrix in a clean environment and coordinate with infra team to allocate ephemeral runners if needed.
migration_plan: 1) Publish js codemod (npx redwood-migrate-shims) + python script to rewrite import usages; 2) Notify customers via changelog + support playbook; 3) Enable opt-in flag in SDK to route to compatibility adapter for one month post-release; 4) Remove adapter after two cycles once telemetry shows <0.1% usage.
